title: Promotion changes a scope, not the operation
takeaway: The next drain reads the promoted scope; an active request continues until it finishes.
assumptions: The example has one pending shared operation and one active exclusive request. Positions are schematic. The active request finishes normally between the second and third frames.

entities.label: Caller scope
entities.summary: Supplies the effective priority used when joining work.

entities.label: Shared read
entities.summary: Starts one operation and tracks separate readers. The last reader's departure signals unfinished work to abort.

entities.label: GitHubWork
entities.summary: Retains the promise and mutable scope. Parent scope references carry promotions into nested work.

entities.label: Scheduler
entities.summary: Selects interactive work first during drain. It allows at most three active tasks, with overlap only for explicitly permitted interactive tasks.

relationships.label: Read and join
relationships.summary: Each read joins the retained work before registering its reader.

relationships.label: Retain work
relationships.summary: The shared operation creates and retains one GitHubWork and returns its promise.

relationships.label: Read scope reference
relationships.summary: The client submits its work scope. The scheduler retains that reference and evaluates effective priority during drain.

plan.question: How does a caller promote existing work, and when does the scheduler use that promotion?
plan.visualApproach: Read left to right from the interactive caller through the shared read and its retained work to the scheduler. Keep the operation and promise fixed. Show the work scope changing, then show pending work entering the active region after the previous request finishes.
plan.whyThisForm: Stable owners and scope-reference connections show why a caller changes existing work rather than creating a second operation.
plan.encodings: Containment shows the scheduler's pending and active regions. A solid connection shows a call; a dashed connection shows a retained scope reference. Labels identify priority and request state.
plan.motion: The caller joins the fixed shared operation and changes its scope to interactive. The active request stays fixed during promotion. After that request finishes, the next drain moves the pending task into the active region.
plan.prediction: If the active exclusive request has not finished, promoted work stays pending even though its effective priority is interactive.
plan.restingState: The same shared operation and scope remain visible, with its task active after selection by the next drain.

scenarios.title: Join, promote, then select
scenarios.input: An interactive caller joins foreground shared work while another exclusive request is active.

frames.title: Existing shared work waits
frames.caption: The shared read retains one work object. The pending task refers to its scope.

frames.title: The caller promotes the same scope
frames.caption: read() joins the work before it registers the reader. Promotion does not call drain or stop the active request.

frames.title: The next drain uses the promotion
frames.caption: When the exclusive request finishes, drain reads the current scope and selects the interactive task.
